transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hey, yeah. Um... well, I guess the main thing is I just get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be trying to work on a job application—which I really need to do, because my roommate is getting kind of annoyed about rent. He actually bought this fancy new espresso machine last week instead of paying his half of the internet bill, which makes zero sense to me. Like, why buy a three-hundred-dollar coffee maker when our Wi-Fi is about to get shut off? We had this huge argument about it in the kitchen... 

But, uh, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. The applications. Yeah, I'll be sitting there trying to fill one out, and then a car drives by outside, or my phone lights up, or I just get some random idea in my head, and suddenly I'm off doing something completely different before I even notice I stopped working on the form. It's just really messing me up.
Have you had a time when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt energized?

Less sleep and still energized? Uh, no, definitely not. If I don't get enough sleep, I am totally wrecked the next day. I mean, I try to get a solid eight hours, but lately, it's been tough because of that roommate I mentioned. He stays up until like 3 AM playing Call of Duty, and he has one of those super loud mechanical keyboards. Just clack clack clack all night right through the wall. 

I actually used to have one of those keyboards when I was in high school. I was super into building computers back then. I spent all my graduation money on a custom rig with all the RGB lights and the water cooling and everything. It was pretty sweet, actually. I kinda miss it, but I had to sell it a few years ago when my Honda broke down and I needed a new alternator. Man, that mechanic totally ripped me off, too, charged me like double what the part was worth... 

But, uh... wait, what was the question? Something about sleeping? Yeah, no, if I miss sleep, I'm just a complete zombie. I definitely don't have extra energy.
Were you having these attention and distractibility problems as a child, before age 12?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Even way back in elementary school it was like this. My teachers were always moving my seat around the classroom because I’d just talk out of turn constantly, or I'd completely forget to bring my homework in. And whenever we had those worksheets, I’d just rush right through them and make a bunch of careless mistakes just to get it over with. I really hated those worksheets, especially the ones where they used a timer? 

Speaking of timers, my mom actually bought me this little tomato-shaped kitchen timer last week to help me focus on my job apps. But the ticking sound was driving me absolutely insane. It sounded exactly like the busted turn signal in my old Honda—the one I had to sell for the alternator? Man, I really loved that car. It had this weird quirk where the radio would only play static if you turned on the AC, so in the summer you either had to sweat or sit in silence. I used to drive it down to the lake with my friends all the time... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, so, the teachers were always getting on my case about my seat and the careless mistakes and stuff. It's pretty much been happening my whole life.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, with symptoms beginning in childhood and persisting into adulthood. He reports marked distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention on tasks, frequent losing track of what he is doing, careless mistakes, and longstanding academic impairment (forgetting homework, talking out of turn, needing seat changes). He denies decreased need for sleep or other manic symptoms, making bipolar disorder unlikely. The pattern is chronic and developmentally early, consistent with F90.0.
